subject: Post-demo: query quality playbook, auth flow, and eval protocol
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wong <elaine@querycraft.io>, Tim Lee <tim.lee@querycraft.io>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: query quality playbook, auth flow, and eval protocol

Hi Elaine / Tim —

Thanks again for joining the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of call (fast):
- Goal: improve query relevance for QueryCraft search verticals (knowledge, product catalog).
- Scope for pilot: 100k query/interaction sample, offline rerank evaluation, then 2-week canary with live routing for top-traffic queries.

Open items / asks from your side:
1) Evaluation dataset: please share a sample of ~5k queries + canonical results where available (CSV or JSONL) and any human judgments/labels. We can accept the sample as a CSV export (column names: query, candidate_id, label).
2) Auth & network: confirm whether you need OIDC (OIDC + SCIM) or API-key bearer tokens for initial integration. We support both; for private deployments we can integrate with your IdP.
3) Production routing policy: do you want per-region routing or a single global endpoint with canary percentage?

Technical notes / recommendations we mentioned on call:
- Reranker strategy: offline eval by NDCG@5 and MRR@10, plus slice-based checks for tail intents (e.g., long-tail queries).
- Top_k guidance: start with top_k=50 for reranker candidate pool; evaluate NDCG@5 and recall@50. For latency-sensitive use cases we recommend top_k=20 as a canary value.
- Structured output/tool-calling: if you plan to use structured card outputs (price/availability), we recommend returning JSONL fields from the reranker stage and using the Redwood structured-output validators to assert schema.

I attached a small evaluation template to make the labeling/eval steps repetitive (redwood_relevance_eval_template.xlsx). I'll also drop a drive folder with a suggested rubric: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQueryCraftEval

Next steps (suggested):
- You: share sample export (CSV) and tell us preferred auth method by end of week.
- Us: prepare an offline eval run and send a short example report (NDCG/MRR + slices) within 3 business days of receiving the sample.
- Schedule: propose a 60-min deep-dive engineering workshop next week to walk through SDK quickstart, routing config, and evaluation artifacts.

Attachments: redwood_relevance_eval_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks —

Kimberly Park

Hi Kimberly —

Really appreciated the demo — good alignment on scope. Answers inline below and attaching a small sample export (querycraft_search_sample.csv).

1) Evaluation dataset: attached is ~5.2k rows exported from our analytics pipeline. Columns are query, candidate_id, current_rank, click, manual_label (sparse). We can provide a larger export if needed.
2) Auth & network: for pilot we prefer API keys (server-to-server bearer tokens). If the pilot progresses to private deployment, we will need OIDC + our Okta team to be involved.
3) Routing: prefer a single global endpoint initially, but would like canary-by-country after pilot.

Questions for you:
- Do you have a recommended format for soft labels vs binary labels in the spreadsheet? We have click data and sparse manual labels.
- Can you share a short SDK quickstart so our infra team can review auth flows?

We can do the 60-min workshop on Thursday (10/22) afternoon PST. Tim and I will both attend.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: query quality playbook, auth flow, and eval protocol

Hi Elaine / Tim —

Thanks for the sample — looks good. A few concrete answers and an SDK snippet you can drop into your infra team's repo.

Labeling format:
- Works well: one row per (query, candidate) with a label column. For soft signals use a score between 0-1 (e.g., normalized clicks or annotator confidence). Keep a separate column for binary accept/reject if you also have manual judgments. Our evaluation template includes mappings to NDCG-ready relevance scores.

Recommended offline eval protocol (practical):
- Candidate generation: generate up to top_k=50 candidates from your current system.
- Rerank: run the reranker over those 50, compute NDCG@5, MRR@10, Recall@50. Also compute per-slice NDCG for long-tail and phrase-match buckets.
- Production canary: start canary with top_k=20 and 5% traffic ramp; measure latency P95 and NDCG delta vs baseline.

Auth & SDK quickstart (Node example):

// Minimal Node.js example - server-side request with API key
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const API_KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY; // server-only secret

async function rerank(query, candidates) {
  const resp = await fetch('https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/rerank', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query, candidates, top_k: 50 })
  });
  return resp.json();
}

Notes: we recommend server-side calls for rerank to avoid exposing keys. For private deployments we can show OIDC flow and short-lived tokens.

Routing snippet (high level):
- Use per-customer policy: default->hosted-standard, canary->hosted-canary (5%). We can provide a JSON policy during the workshop.

Eval artifacts: I uploaded an example offline-report generator to the shared drive and wired the eval template to output NDCG/MRR slices: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQueryCraftEval

If helpful, we'll run a demo offline evaluation on the sample and share a short PDF report before the workshop.

Kimberly / Marissa — can you confirm Thurs 10/22 2pm PST for the 60-min workshop?

-Karthik
